extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students in media/communication research, especially those studying news selection and audience behavior
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly empirical study of how news factors and formal article characteristics influence recipients' media use and selection of articles. Uses content analysis and audience diary data to compare articles used vs not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: News factors as selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: News factors indicate relevance and thus are plausible selection criteria that allow for an efficient reduction of world complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on cognitive psychology (psychology of attention), news factors are effective because they signal relevance to recipients; the paper investigates this empirically using content analysis and audience diary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for articles of high news value
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents prefer articles of high news value to articles of low news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bivariate analyses of the news factors in articles used and articles not used indicate that news factors influence media use. This is an observed tendency but is qualified by multivariate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal characteristics of articles as determinants of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Not so much the news factors but rather the formal characteristics of an article determine selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multivariate analyses in the study qualified the bivariate result by showing formal/article-level characteristics have a stronger influence on whether recipients select an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formal characteristics as shortcuts for judging relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients might use formal characteristics as shortcuts for judging the relevance of an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion focuses on whether formal features (unspecified in the abstract) serve as heuristics that allow recipients to quickly assess an article's perceived relevance, rather than processing full news-factor content.
